query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a silicide coating to a refractory high-entropy alloy substrate will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Preparation of Si-20Cr-20Fe (wt.%) coating via fused slurry method
generation.structural_mediator: Double-layer structure formed: outer high-silicon layer (MSi₂) and inner low-silicon layer (M₅Si₃)
generation.mechanism: Silicidation and diffusion reactions occurred on the surface of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate; disilicide has the best stability due to enthalpy of formation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance due to the formation of a stable silicide coating
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 1000°C - 1500°C, atmosphere: air or oxygen-rich environment
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature range and atmosphere conditions under which the silicide coating will be effective are uncertain and require further experimentation

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the silicide-coated sample shows no significant improvement in high-temperature oxygen resistance compared to the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: MoNbTaTiW Refractory High-Entropy Alloy (RHEA) substrate. Intervention: Preparation of Si-20Cr-20Fe (wt.%) coating via fused slurry method. Processing: Powders milled, mixed with 4% polyethylene alcohol binder, immersed, dried at 80°C, then vacuum oven at 1430°C for 1 h under 5 × 10⁻³ Pa. Test conditions: As-prepared state (before oxidation). Structure change: Double-layer structure formed: outer high-silicon layer (MSi₂) and inner low-silicon layer (M₅Si₃); total thickness ~113 µm. Mechanism: Silicidation and diffusion reactions occurred on the surface of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate; disilicide has the best stability due to enthalpy of formation. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi 2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M 5 Si 3 as the inner layer."
